resolutions.researcher_notes: operating supported by 2 independent sources: Wikipedia (East–West Pipeline is an operating Aramco line, commissioned early 1980s and still in service) and Saudipedia ('Saudi Aramco developed and operates the infrastructure'). Techint (contractor) also describes the line as having 'started operations'. No source suggests shut/mothballed.

Fuel=Gas supported by 2 independent sources. Techint (builder) titles it the Shedgum–Yanbu 'Gas Pipeline'; Saudipedia describes a 'natural gas liquids (NGL) pipeline'. This line carries NGL, which GGIT categorizes under Gas — consistent with value.

StartYear1=1978. Techint (contractor) frames 1978 as the start: published 2023-07-14, '45 years after this 1,166-km Gas Pipeline started operations' → 1978, and 1978 is confirmed by Saudipedia as the year construction began. CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: Saudipedia and the Aramco literature put the NGL line's in-service date at 1981, and Wikipedia gives 'commissioned 1982'. So 1978 is best read as project/construction start, not commissioning; if the field means operational start, 1981 is better supported.

LengthKnown=1200 km matches Wikipedia's 1,201 km (746 mi) for the East–West corridor. CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: sources dedicated to the gas/NGL line give a slightly shorter figure — Techint 1,166 km and Saudipedia 1,170 km. The 1200 value tracks the overall Petroline corridor length rather than the ~1,166–1,170 km dedicated gas line.

Diameter=48 in supported by Wikipedia: 'The pipeline has two pipes, one 56 inches (142 cm) in diameter and the other, originally for natural gas liquids, 48 inches (122 cm) in diameter.' The 48-inch line is the NGL/gas line, matching this row. Single strong source; other outlets echo 48-inch but trace to the same lineage.

FuelSource=Abqaiq supported by Wikipedia: the pipeline 'runs from the Abqaiq oil field in the Eastern Province'. Note Techint and Saudipedia name Shedgum (the Shedgum gas plant) as the origin — Abqaiq and Shedgum are adjacent facilities in the same Eastern Province gas-processing complex feeding this line, so the two names refer to the same origin area.

Start=Eastern Province, End=Yanbu supported by 2 independent sources. Wikipedia: 'from the Abqaiq oil field in the Eastern Province ... to Yanbu at the Red Sea.' Saudipedia: Shedgum (Eastern Province) to Yanbu on the western/Red Sea coast. Yanbu (Yanbu al Bahr) is in Al Madinah Province, matching EndState/Province.

Operator=أرامكو السعودية (Saudi Aramco) supported by 2 independent sources. Saudipedia: 'Saudi Aramco developed and operates the infrastructure.' Wikipedia refers to 'Saudi Aramco's East-West Pipeline'. Sources are English; the field value is the Arabic name for Saudi Aramco.

Owner1=Saudi Aramco 100% supported by 2 independent sources. Saudipedia states Saudi Aramco developed and operates the line; Wikipedia describes it as 'Saudi Aramco's East-West Pipeline'. No co-owners reported; sole state-oil-company ownership is consistent with 100%.
